steps.content:
The baseline (excluding `d7I`) shows no persistent shift — its post-9/22 mean ($8292) is within normal noise of the pre-9/22 mean ($8253, std ~$51). The entire sustained anomaly is the new application `d7I`, which first appears exactly on 2025-09-22 under AWS service `l5O5g` with nine instance families contributing ~$539/day.

**Root cause analysis summary:**
- Account `tVENWJP` daily cost jumped from ~$8,250/day to ~$8,800/day starting **2025-09-22** and stayed elevated.
- Decomposition by CSP shows AWS +$538/day; by service, `l5O5g` +$535/day; by application, **`d7I` = +$540.68/day**, a brand-new application with zero cost before 9/22.
- `d7I` consists of nine instance families (JvKGRn9oaQ, LzGJ9rhJoA, QHfxsO7Tbi, C4JJjdjpR2, q10uAtDIqF, 9JSKdPztdB, PvjSNbcfQ1, EeqjKx3K5D, nbJ0X8TQ4n) — all newly launched on 9/22. These are all part of the single new application `d7I`; the root cause resource is the application itself.
- No price changes occurred anywhere (all instance families have a single constant price), and no other resource begins or ends on 9/22. The residual day-over-day difference is ordinary instance-count noise (baseline mean unchanged).
- The `VFRAe4nYaW` (application `GmI`) spike begins 2025-10-13, unrelated to the 9/22 anomaly.
